body.statement:
For every \(M\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) and every integer \(0\le k\le\lfloor T/2\rfloor\), put \(\overline\theta_k=(T-k)^{-1}\sum_{t=k+1}^{T}Z_t(k)\).  Then
\[
 \left|E_M[Z_t(k)]-\theta(K,e)\right|\le2M_1q_C\alpha^k
\]
and
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_M(\overline\theta_k)
 \le\frac1{T-k}\left\{M_2L^{k+1}
 +4M_2\sum_{r=1}^{k}L^r
 +\frac{4M_1\sqrt{M_2}\,\alpha^k}{1-\alpha}\right\}.
\]
where the sum is zero when \(k=0\).  Consequently the clipped estimator satisfies
\[
 E_M[(\widehat\theta_k-\theta(K,e))^2]
 \le4M_1^2q_C^2\alpha^{2k}+\operatorname{Var}_M(\overline\theta_k).
\]
body.proof_tex:
Write \(m(s,a):=E_K[Y_t\mid S_t=s,A_t=a]\).  The conditional moment envelope \(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}reward}\) gives \(|m(s,a)|\le M_1\) and \(E_K[Y_t^2\mid S_t=s,A_t=a]\le M_2\); hence \(|g_e(s)|\le M_1\).  Sequential randomization in \(\mathrm{ass{:}sequential\text{-}ignorability}\), followed by the kernel factorization in \(\mathrm{ass{:}pomdp\text{-}kernel}\), permits cancellation of each behavior action probability against the corresponding factor \(\rho_j\).  Since \(S_{t-k}\sim d_b\) by \(\mathrm{ass{:}stationary\text{-}start}\), this gives, equation by equation,
\[
 E_M[Z_t(k)]=d_bP_e^kg_e,
 \qquad
 \theta(K,e)=d_eP_e^kg_e,
\]
where the second equality uses stationarity \(d_eP_e^k=d_e\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}target\text{-}value}\).

If \(C=1\), \(d_e\le d_b\) and equality of total masses imply \(d_e=d_b\).  If \(C>1\), define
\[
 \nu:=\frac{Cd_b-d_e}{C-1}.
\]
The pointwise overlap assumption makes \(\nu\) nonnegative, and normalization of \(d_b,d_e\) gives \(\nu(\mathcal S)=1\).  Thus
\[
 d_b=C^{-1}d_e+q_C\nu,
 \qquad
 \|d_b-d_e\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=q_C\|\nu-d_e\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le q_C. \tag{1}
\]
Iterating \(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}contraction}\) under \(P_e\), and using that a function bounded by \(M_1\) changes expectations by at most \(2M_1\) times total variation, yields
\[
 |d_bP_e^kg_e-d_eP_e^kg_e|
 \le2M_1\|d_bP_e^k-d_eP_e^k\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le2M_1q_C\alpha^k. \tag{2}
\]

We next prove the variance bound without a support bound on \(Y_t\).  The policy-overlap assumption gives \(0\le\rho_j\le L\) and hence \(\rho_j^2\le L\rho_j\).  Applying this inequality to all \(k+1\) ratios and then cancelling the remaining ratios as above gives
\[
 E_M[Z_t(k)^2]\le M_2L^{k+1}. \tag{3}
\]
For \(1\le h\le k\), the two weight windows overlap in exactly \(k+1-h\) actions.  Replace the square of every shared ratio by \(L\rho\).  The remaining product of one ratio for each action in the union changes the behavior actions on that union to target actions and therefore defines a probability law.  Cauchy--Schwarz under that hybrid law, together with the pointwise conditional second-moment bound at the two reward times, gives
\[
 E_M[|Z_t(k)Z_{t+h}(k)|]\le M_2L^{k+1-h}. \tag{4}
\]
Also \(|E_MZ_t(k)|\le M_1\), by its representation as \(d_bP_e^kg_e\).  Because \(M_1^2<M_2\) and \(L^{k+1-h}\ge1\), (4) implies
\[
 |\operatorname{Cov}_M(Z_t(k),Z_{t+h}(k))|
 \le2M_2L^{k+1-h},\qquad1\le h\le k. \tag{5}
\]

For \(h\ge k+1\), condition on the full history through \((Y_t,S_{t+1})\).  The Markov property and likelihood-ratio cancellation on the future block give
\[
 E_M[Z_{t+h}(k)\mid S_{t+1}]
 =\psi_h(S_{t+1}),
 \qquad
 \psi_h:=P_b^{h-k-1}P_e^kg_e. \tag{6}
\]
Under behavior stationarity, \(E_M\psi_h(S_{t+1})=d_bP_e^kg_e=E_MZ_t(k)\).  For every Markov kernel whose Dobrushin coefficient is at most \(\alpha\), the oscillation inequality \(\operatorname{osc}(Pf)\le\alpha\operatorname{osc}(f)\) follows by applying the total-variation contraction to two point masses.  Applying it to all \(h-1\) kernels in (6) gives
\[
 \operatorname{osc}(\psi_h)\le2M_1\alpha^{h-1}. \tag{7}
\]
Moreover, cancellation of one copy of each ratio and Cauchy--Schwarz give
\[
 E_M|Z_t(k)|
 =E_{\mathrm{hyb}}|Y_t|
 \le\{E_{\mathrm{hyb}}Y_t^2\}^{1/2}\le\sqrt{M_2}. \tag{8}
\]
Combining (6)--(8), and using that the mean of \(\psi_h(S_{t+1})\) lies between its minimum and maximum, yields
\[
 |\operatorname{Cov}_M(Z_t(k),Z_{t+h}(k))|
 \le2M_1\sqrt{M_2}\,\alpha^{h-1},\qquad h\ge k+1. \tag{9}
\]
This is the required disjoint-window control; it uses \(M_1\sqrt{M_2}\), not the false implication \(E|Z_t(k)|\le M_1\).

Let \(N=T-k\).  Stationarity and the covariance decomposition, followed by (3), (5), and (9), give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Var}_M(\overline\theta_k)
 &\le\frac1N\left\{M_2L^{k+1}
 +4M_2\sum_{h=1}^{k}L^{k+1-h}
 +4M_1\sqrt{M_2}\sum_{h=k+1}^{\infty}\alpha^{h-1}\right\}\\
 &=\frac1N\left\{M_2L^{k+1}
 +4M_2\sum_{r=1}^{k}L^r
 +\frac{4M_1\sqrt{M_2}\,\alpha^k}{1-\alpha}\right\}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{10}
\]
Finally, \(|\theta(K,e)|\le M_1\) by the conditional mean envelope.  Projection onto \([-M_1,M_1]\) cannot increase squared distance from \(\theta(K,e)\).  Combining (2), the identity \(E[(\overline\theta_k-\theta)^2]=\operatorname{Var}(\overline\theta_k)+(E\overline\theta_k-\theta)^2\), and (10) proves all three conclusions.
body.justification: This gives the radius-sensitive observable upper bound under the published conditional first- and second-moment envelope.
body.gap: The calculation retains the normalized latent-overlap radius and controls overlapping and disjoint windows without a bounded-support shortcut.
body.consumer: It supplies the attaining half of the uniform overlap frontier.
